messages.content: What is the largest planet in the universe?

function.name: space_star_info
function.description: Retrieve information about a particular star in the universe. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

information.description: The type of information needed about the star.

message.content:
The largest planet that astronomers have confirmed so far is **HD 100546 b**.  
It orbits the young star HD 100546, about 320 light‑years from Earth, and is still in the process of forming (a “protoplanet”). Its radius is roughly **2.5–3 times that of Jupiter** (≈ 200,000 km), making it the biggest planet we’ve been able to measure directly.

> *Key facts*  
> • **Name:** HD 100546 b  
> • **Radius:** ~ 2.5–3 R_J (≈ 200,000 km)  
> • **Mass:** ~ 10–20 M_J (though the exact value is uncertain because it’s still accreting material)  
> • **Distance from host star:** ~ 10 AU (about the distance of Saturn from the Sun)  
> • **Age:** The system is only a few million years old, so the planet is still growing.

Because the universe is vast and we have only observed a tiny fraction of its planets, it’s possible that even larger planets exist elsewhere. However, as of now, HD 100546 b holds the record for the largest known planet.
